newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban claim advances in northwest Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Taleban claim advances in northwest Afghanistan.

text.p: The Islamic Taleban militia said its forces had advanced against those of Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum in northwestern Afghanistan on Saturday.

A Taleban spokesman in Kandahar, contacted by the Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) agency, said Taleban fighters had captured Bala Murghab district in Badghis province and would now try to seize Ghormach, a town near the adjacent province of Faryab.
He said at least two Taleban fighters had been killed and 12 wounded in the clashes, adding that five soldiers loyal to Dostum had been killed. The fighting had subsided by dark.
The spokesman said at least 3,000 Taleban fighters had been thrown into the battle for Badghis, where some towns and districts have changed hands several times in the past few days.
There was no immediate word on the fighting from the Dostum camp, now allied with ousted government commander Ahmad Shah Masood against the Taleban rulers of Kabul.
The battle for Badghis, a relatively remote province, is important because success there for the Taleban could open up an invasion route into Dostum's northern heartland.
On the other hand, a Taleban defeat in Badghis could lay open the western city of Herat to attack by Dostum and forces loyal to the city's former governor Ismail Khan.

Khan, who fled to neighbouring Iran when Herat fell to the Taleban in September last year, is reported to have sent hundreds of fighters in aircraft provided by Dostum to the town of Maimana in Faryab province to attack the Taleban.
Herat is populated mainly by Tajiks, the same ethnic group to which Masood and ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani belong. The Taleban draw most of their support from ethnic Pashtuns.
